(1) a combination of IR along with the consistency based subset evaluation technique provides the best prediction accuracy; (2) size and complexity metrics are not good indicators of real-time software defects; (3) the best predictor model is dependent upon the software defect data sets used for training and testing.

the combination of instance-based reasoning and instance-based learning with consistency-based subset evaluation provides better consistency in accuracy compared to other models and the "size" and complexity metrics are not sufficient to predict the defects in real-time software.

there are no best predictor model and best metrics for software defect prediction.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best predictor model is dependent upon the data set and the nature of the data set, and that the accuracy of the prediction model can be improved by using multiple models.
the accuracy of the prediction model depends on the data set, the type of software being predicted, the size of the software being predicted, and the metrics used to train the prediction model.
the accuracy of the prediction models is not only a function of the predictor model, but is also highly dependent on the data set and metrics used.

the best model for software defects prediction may vary based on the data set and the metrics used for prediction.
there is no one best predictor for all software defect prediction problems and the choice of predictor model depends on the type of data set and the type of defects to be predicted.
